subject: Maths
title: Percentage change
subtitle: Fractions, Decimals and Percentages · GCSE Maths
learning_objective: I can calculate percentage increase, decrease and percentage change.

key_vocab.definition: Percentage change measures how much a value has increased or decreased as a percentage of the original.

sections.title: Learning Objective
sections.content: I can calculate percentage increase, decrease and percentage change.

sections.title: Key Words
sections.content: Percentage change -- Percentage change measures how much a value has increased or decreased as a percentage of the original.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
% change = (new − old) ÷ old × 100. Positive = increase, negative = decrease.
change ÷ original × 100 = % change
Always divide by ORIGINAL

Key examples:
  ✓ £20 → £25 = +25%  (increase)
  ✓ £40 → £30 = −25%  (decrease)
  ✓ 10 → 12 = +20%  ((2÷10)×100)
  ✗ £20 → £30 = +33%  (should be +50%)
  ✗ Divide by NEW value  (always divide by ORIGINAL)

sections.title: Worked Example
sections.content:
Example 1 – increase
  Price rises from £40 to £50. Find the % increase.
  Change = 50 − 40 = 10
  10 ÷ 40 = 0.25
  0.25 × 100 = 25%
  = 25% increase
  (Always divide the change by the ORIGINAL price (£40).)

Example 2 – decrease
  Population drops from 800 to 600. Find the % decrease.
  Change = 800 − 600 = 200
  200 ÷ 800 = 0.25
  0.25 × 100 = 25%
  = 25% decrease
  (The change is always positive; the ‘decrease’ describes the direction.)

sections.title: % increase
sections.content:
Calculate the percentage increase. Use (change ÷ old) × 100.

(a) £20 → £25
(b) £40 → £50
(c) 60 → 90
(d) 200 → 240

sections.title: Word problems
sections.content:
State whether each is an increase or decrease, and find the %.

(a) Salary £25k → £30k
(b) Houses 400 → 480
(c) Bill £80 → £64
(d) Speed 50 → 35 mph

sections.title: Mixed % change
sections.content:
Find the percentage change. State increase or decrease.

(a) 12 → 15
(b) £90 → £108
(c) 60 → 45
(d) £500 → £575
(e) 120 → 90

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
✓ £20 → £25 is a 25% increase
✗ Divide by the new value, not the old
✓ £100 → £80 is a 20% decrease
✗ 200 → 240 is a 40% increase
✓ % change can be negative for a decrease
